    Unlock Tessellate

    Install the certificate

    Do this once per phone, so this address is trusted and never warns again.

    iPhone: press Install the certificate in Safari and choose Allow. Then, in the iPhone's own Settings app, General, VPN and Device Management, Tessellate, Install. Then General, About, Certificate Trust Settings, and switch it on.

    Android: open the downloaded file from the phone's own system settings app: Security, Encryption and credentials, Install a certificate, CA certificate.

    The first time this phone signs in, the computer the notebook is on asks whether to let it in: choose Allow there, and the phone opens by itself (it waits up to three minutes).

    Forgot your password?

    Ordinary notes, documents, boards and settings are not encrypted with your password, so neither path touches them. Private notes are: only your password or your recovery key opens them.

    With the recovery key you choose a new password and keep every private note. The key you used stops working and a new one is shown once, so save that one too. Every other open session is signed out.

    Without it, a reset clears the password so you can set a new one. Private notes stay sealed for good; a sealed backup still opens with its own password. You need a six-digit code that Tessellate prints in the terminal it runs in (or its log file, when there is no terminal), valid for ten minutes, one use. "Allow other devices on this network" is turned off. Either way it can only be done on this computer.

    Reset your password on the computer this notebook lives on. Another device can't do it.

    Set a new password with the key you saved. Private notes are kept.

    A reset keeps notes, documents, boards and settings. Private notes are lost for good, because only your password or recovery key opens them; a sealed backup keeps its own password.

    In a terminal, in the app's folder:

    python -m tessellate --reset-password

    Or reset here. A six-digit code is printed in the terminal where Tessellate is running, or in its log file if it has no terminal, so only someone at this computer can reset.

    Your recovery key

    If you forget your password, "Forgot your password?" on the lock screen takes this key and a new password, and keeps your private notes. Without it, a reset leaves them sealed for good.

    The app never stores the key, so it can't show it again. Making a new one in Settings, Account & security replaces it, and the old one stops working.

    Download .txt asks where to save it. In the desktop app the Save dialog starts in Documents and refuses the notebook's own folder, since a key beside the notebook opens it for anyone who copies it.

    Forget your password, and a recovery key sets a new one with your private notes kept. Recommended.

    Save it somewhere away from this computer, such as a password manager or on paper. It is shown only this once.

    Atlas

    Explains the app, never your notes.

    Ask how anything in the app works

    Answers come from the app's own help. Atlas cannot read your notes or your documents.

    Atlas is named for a book of maps: it is the reference you open to find your way around this app. Quick "how do I…" answers about Tessellate itself, not your notes, and nothing here is saved. It answers on your utility model while smart model routing is on, on the chat model while it is off, and Settings, Models can give the guide a model of its own.

    Agent

    Ctrl+Shift+A opens and closes this from any tab, or use Agent in the status bar. Enter sends, Shift+Enter starts a line, Down moves into the starters and Escape closes. It uses the same model, tools and notebook the Chat tab does, so anything it writes or files is real, and it answers from what you have written; tick the box below to hand it whatever you have open. It remembers this conversation until you press Start over. With no model it still runs: every starter answers from your notes, and an act (remind me, tag, link, add to today's note) comes as a card you confirm and can undo. A plan it draws waits for Run the plan, each step's writes listed; Stop ends it between two steps, and Ctrl+Z takes back its last write. The paperclip, a drop or a paste adds files as chips (any kind, up to four); nothing is saved until you send, and the x on a chip takes one back. On a phone it opens as a sheet from More.

    It can read and search your notes, write and file new ones, and set reminders.

    Find anything

    Every kind of thing you keep here is searched at once, by the words you typed and by what they mean, so a note that says the same thing in different words still comes back. Each result says which of the two found it.

    Narrow it with operators, alone or together:

    • tag:recipes things tagged recipes
    • in:work only the Work space
    • kind:chat one kind: note, document, board, map, file, bookmark, reminder, chat or recording
    • before:2026-01 and after:2025-06-30 by the day it was written
    • has:image with an image, a file, a link, a reminder or a highlight
    • is:pinned pinned, archived, done, open or a draft
    • "exact phrase" those words in that order
    • -word leaves out anything that says it

    Up and Down walk the results, Enter opens one, Escape closes. The star saves the search as a row in the Notes sidebar. The suggestions under the box close on Escape, on a click outside them, or when you scroll the results behind.

    When nothing matches, the box says what it searched and offers one way on: every kind when a kind is chosen, the word spelled as the dictionary has it, or the nearest feature by name.

    Activity

    Running lists every job the app is doing now (indexing, a model loading or answering, imports, reading text, transcribing, backups, the agent) with Stop where a job can stop part way, and every model call is one of them. Under it, what finished in the last half hour says how it ended, how long it took and when, with its lines. Stop the model, in the menu, ends any answer and lets the model leave memory. Agent runs lists each run this session with its steps; the log is in the menu.

                    Tessellate

                    Today at a glance: your recent notes, reminders and widgets. Search finds notes, documents, files and app actions, and Ctrl+K opens the command palette for commands and places. Get started lists the first steps, ticked as you finish them; its menu can mark them all done or hide it, and Customise, Show Get started (or the palette's Show Get started) brings it back. Customise, then Edit layout, lets you add, move, resize and remove widgets. In the Focused view the greeting card shows what is due today, your meetings, the notes to file and the note you were last in.

                          Options

                          Capture a thought

                          A note is plain text. These few things do something extra:

                          • [[its first few words]], links to another note. Start typing [[ and a list of your notes appears; pick one to complete it. The link becomes a clickable chip on the saved note.
                          • # A title on the first line becomes the note's title: the same thing the "Optional title" box above writes for you.
                          • **bold**, *italic*, `code`, ~~struck~~, ==highlight== (or ==green|highlight==, also blue, pink, purple, orange; or select the words and use the button), [text](url) and $x^2$ all render on the saved note.
                          • #word anywhere in the text tags the note with that word when it is saved (#project/garden nests). The tags field below takes them too, comma separated.

                          Two things worth knowing, because they are easy to assume and both untrue:

                          • / after a space or at a line's start opens the blocks menu (also Ctrl+/); pressing / anywhere you are not typing jumps to the search box.
                          • Headings beyond the first line, lists, tables, fenced code and > [!tip] callouts are stored faithfully but are not rendered on a note card, a note list rendered that way gets very tall very fast. They do render in the document editor.

                          Writing room

                          Type whatever's in your head, half sentences are fine. Atlas turns it into a draft as it writes it. Pick what to write, in what voice and at what length, and hand it notes you already have to write from.

                          Your own words stay in the box: nothing here overwrites what you typed, Undo steps back through every pass, and every draft Atlas produced is kept under the box so you can go back to one. Drafting and Refine need a model connected: with none, pressing them says so and offers Set up a model, and everything else on this tab still works. Suggest a title takes the title from your own words, and Split into notes cuts the text at its headings and paragraphs.

                          Ask your notebook

                          Switch on: your model writes the answer from your notes, citing them, and a From your notes line under it opens the quoted answer to the same question beside it. Off: the answer is From your notes, with no AI. The app picks the sentences in your notes that answer the question and strings them together: the answer on the first line, then the other notes joined by how they relate (also, later, separately, or but when two may disagree), a timeline for a when question, two sides for a comparison, and a few questions to ask next. Tell me more, or the second one, follows on from the answer before.

                          Every sentence in it is quoted from a note and cited; the only words the app adds are the joining ones and the counts and dates it measured. It never answers yes or no for you, and it says which of your words none of the notes found mention. With no model running the switch labelled AI beside the answer length is off and greyed, its hover text and the notice below name why, and the answer is From your notes; it comes back when a model does.

                                The filter understands a few shortcuts, all of these work without any AI:

                                • bread proving, both words, in any order
                                • "proving times", that exact phrase
                                • tag:work or #work, only notes carrying that tag (and its nested tags, like work/meetings)
                                • cat:recipes or in:recipes, only that category
                                • title:budget, a word in the note's title
                                • before:2026-09-01, after:2026-08, by the day it was written
                                • is:favourite, your starred notes (is:pinned still works); also is:private, is:linked, is:untagged, is:draft, and is:review, the filings to check (Atlas's estimate is under 50%, or it left it in Uncategorised), each with Accept, Refile and Split
                                • tags:<2, fewer than 2 tags (also <=, >, >=, or a bare number for exactly that many)
                                • has:link, has:file, has:image or has:reminder, notes that carry one; space:work, only that space; kind:note, asked of the search engine
                                • -picnic, notes that do not mention it
                                • type:meeting, prop:status=open, prop:effort>2, a note's properties; links:[[Kiln plan]], rel:supports, entity:"Sam Lee", its links and the people and things it names (a - before any leaves those out). A bar then offers the same notes as a Table or on the graph

                                      to

                                      A note sits where it is about when it says so, "the deadline is next Friday" plots on that Friday, marked with a clock, and at when it was written otherwise. The feed opens on today with the week ahead above it (scroll up), and an empty day ahead has an Add for a reminder or an event. Arrow keys walk the rows, Enter opens one where it sits. The strip below shows the last seven days: a dot marks a day with a page, and pressing a day opens its page or starts it. The arrows beside the month walk a week, and the month opens a calendar to jump to any earlier day. In the feed, Ctrl and the mouse wheel, or a pinch, makes the date groups finer or coarser, as do + and - on a row. The thin strip at the feed's right edge shows how much you wrote over the whole range, labelled by month or year (Options, Dates beside the strip, hides the labels); click or drag it to jump. The chips under the strip show what you wrote on today's date in earlier years, and the year menu beside the month narrows the list to one year; Options, Time range, On this day does the same.

                                      The calendar shows a month, a week or a day: reminders and meetings at their time, a day's page at the top of its day and a chip with its title for each note (a dot each where a day is too short; a note that names a second date shows an arrow chip there). Press a day to open it as a Day view; a +n opens the day in the feed. Drag a reminder to another day or hour to move it, or press Alt and an arrow on it (Undo puts it back). Arrows walk the days, Page Up and Page Down the months, T is today, Enter or Space opens the day (from a Day view, in the feed). Double-click a day or an hour, or press Add or N, to add a reminder or an event there (an event is a meeting note, with a reminder at its start).

                                      Drag a note to move it. Let go and it settles near where you put it. Double-click a note to pin it in place (a pinned note keeps its place when you come back); double-click it again to let it go.

                                      This map is built for you from what your notes already say. If you want to draw one yourself, your own cards, your own links, your own arrangement, that is a mind map, and the button in the toolbar opens them.

                                      Solid lines are links you made, dashed lines are trains of thought, dotted lines are notes that mean similar things. Hover a note to spotlight its connections and see its card (dates, links, views, properties and tags; the arrow keys show it too), scroll or use the buttons to zoom, click a note to edit it right here (Open, Focus, Pin and Link at its foot, the rest under ), and click a legend colour to hide that category. Double-click empty space to add a note there. Gravity and Spread reshape whatever you have not placed yourself. A Tree, Radial, Arc or Treemap layout stays still and is named in the toolbar; click its name to change it. Treemap sizes each category by how many notes it holds. A bigger dot has more links; Size in the options changes what size means, and the legend says which. Drop one note onto another to link them, and use Trace to see how any two notes connect.

                                      View

                                      Layout is how the notes are placed: Force lets links pull them together, Tree, Radial and Arc lay them out from one note, and Treemap boxes them by category.

                                      Shape is Force's own: Organic follows the links, Clusters gathers each category, Galaxy puts the best-connected notes in the middle.

                                      Colour paints the dots by category, topic, note type, age, tag or another rule; Size makes a dot bigger for more connections, a longer note or a more recent one.

                                      Match strength appears while Similarity (under Show) is on: raise it to keep only the closest matches.

                                      Focus
                                      Physics

                                      These shape the Force layout; under Tree, Radial, Arc and Treemap they are dimmed.

                                      • Gravity: how hard every note is drawn toward the middle, so the map packs tighter or spreads wider.
                                      • Spread: how far apart linked notes sit.
                                      • Link force: how hard each link pulls its two notes together.
                                      • Length by similarity: notes that match more closely in meaning sit nearer each other.
                                      • Group by category: each category gathers in a place of its own, and a note with no links sits with its category.
                                      • Unpin all lets the notes you pinned move again, and Reshuffle layout lays the map out again from a new start.
                                      Show

                                      An entity is a person, place or thing Atlas found named across your notes, drawn as its own node joined to every note that mentions it.

                                      Documents adds a node for each document your notes are attached to, and Boards adds one for each mind map or whiteboard, joined to the notes on it.

                                      Tags and Attachments add a node for each tag and each file or picture, joined to its notes. Unwritten links draws each [[name]] no note answers to as a faint node; click it to write that note.

                                      Similarity joins each note to its two closest matches in meaning with a faint dashed line: the stronger the match, the darker the line. Solid lines are links you or Atlas made. Point at a note to see how close each match is, and raise Match strength (under Size) to keep only the closest.

                                      Display

                                      These change how the map is drawn, never what is on it.

                                      • Labels: a short name under every note; off, a name shows only when you point at it.
                                      • Curved links: links bend gently instead of running straight.
                                      • Cluster glow: a faint wash of colour behind each cluster.
                                      • Label backgrounds: a plate behind each name, so a line under it stops at its edge.
                                      • Arrows: a spark on each link, pointing away from the note that made it.
                                      • Fit on view change: the map is framed again when you change layout or resize.
                                      • Text fade: to the right, names stay visible from further out on a big map.
                                      • Link thickness: how thick the lines are.
                                      Filter

                                      Kinds of link: each chip is one kind of line on the map. Press it to hide that kind, and press it again to bring it back.

                                      Properties: each chip is a value some of your notes carry. Press it to light those notes and dim the rest; the lit chip is outlined, and pressing it again clears the light.

                                      Kinds of link: press one to hide it; a struck-through kind is hidden

                                      Properties: press one to light its notes; the lit one is outlined

                                      Time

                                      The slider hides every note made after the date it points at, so the map shows your notebook as it was then. All the way right shows everything.

                                      Play moves the slider forward from the start, so the notes appear in the order you made them.

                                      All Time
                                      Groups

                                      Type some words and press Add: every note that matches them takes one colour, and the group is listed in the legend. A note you write later that matches joins the group by itself.

                                      A group's colour wins over the Colour setting for its notes. Press the x beside a group to remove it; the notes go back to their usual colour.

                                      Minimap

                                      The minimap is a small picture of the whole map in one corner, with a box for the part you are looking at. Click or drag on it to move the view.

                                      Position picks the corner, or Off hides it. Size makes it small or large.

                                                        Your reminders

                                                        Reminders are grouped as overdue, today and upcoming. Write one in plain words: the day, time, repeat and early alert it was read as show as chips under the box (press one to leave it as words), and Enter adds it; with no time it asks for one. A repeat can be every weekday, every 2 weeks or the last Friday of the month, and "1 day before" adds an alert ahead of the due time. Or use Quick set. The date and time fields open a month and the day's times, and read a typed day such as next friday. Notifications fire while a tab is open, even in the background, with Done and Snooze on them; the desktop app notifies with its window closed. Calendar opens the Timeline's calendar with only reminders, where one drags to another day. A reminder's menu also opens Google Calendar or Outlook with it filled in, only when you press it. More adds every open reminder to your calendar app, or imports a calendar file as reminders. Tell the chat "I need to call the dentist on Friday" and a Make this a reminder chip appears under the reply.

                                                        Notifications are blocked.

                                                        A due reminder still chimes and shows here; only the system notification is off. To allow it:

                                                        Chrome and Edge: the icon left of the address, then Notifications, Allow.

                                                        Firefox: the icon left of the address, then clear Notifications blocked, and reload.

                                                        Safari: its own Settings (Websites, then Notifications), then Allow for this site.

                                                        The desktop app: your system's notification settings for Tessellate.

                                                        Documents

                                                        A document is a longer piece of writing with its own editor, outline and history. Open one to keep writing. Import a file, in the more menu, turns a Word file, PDF, spreadsheet, Markdown or code file into a document you can edit. The property menu narrows the list to documents that carry a given front matter value, and the more menu sets how many show per page.

                                                          Every action has one place. Click a topic and its ring says what you can do to it from here: add a topic under it, add one beside it, fold it, delete it, connect it to another, and More for the rest.

                                                          The strip under the bar is how the topic and its line look: bold, core idea, size, colour, icon, shape and the line's own weight. A topic's colour is also a menu away: right-click it, More, Topic colour (Branch colour past the first trunk). Right-click a line for what only a line has: reverse it, label it, cut it. Double-click a line to label it, and its grip to straighten it. More, Branch draws a boundary round a branch or summarises a topic (select several side by side to summarise them together); More, Topic, Comment… starts a thread on it. More, Look copies a topic's style, pastes it, or gives it to every topic at its level; View, How this map looks sets the hierarchy and each level. View, Present branches shows the map one branch at a time; Esc ends it.

                                                          The canvas itself: double-click it for a new trunk, right-click it for the map's own menu. Escape takes back a drag you have not let go of yet; Shift+1 fits the whole map and Ctrl+0 shows it at 100%. The canvas's own background colour is in View, in the top bar, and PNG or SVG export keeps whatever it is set to.

                                                          This rail is the map itself: a new trunk, focus on one branch, the layout and a tidy. Every ring slot is also a key, so Tab adds a topic under the selected one, Enter one beside it, C folds, Delete removes, Shift and C connects, and Shift and F10 opens the topic's own menu.

                                                                  Recordings

                                                                  Everything recorded in the app: meetings, lectures and voice notes. Search finds a recording by its name or by what was said in it; a hit shows the line, and pressing it plays from there. The audio is saved every 10 seconds while it records, so closing the tab keeps all but the last few seconds, and the next start says "Recording recovered".

                                                                  Play at 0.5 to 2x; press or drag the waveform to jump, the line on it and the time beside it say where you are. Press M or the pin to mark the playhead with an optional comment (M or Marker while recording marks the moment too); each mark under the player plays from its time and opens the transcript at that line. Download audio in the ⋯ saves the file. Trim keeps a part as a new recording; the original stays until you empty the bin. Delete puts a recording in the bin. Transcribe in the ⋯ runs in the background: the card shows how far it is with a Stop, and a notification says when it is done. Once transcribed, Transcript lists its lines with their times: press one to play from that moment, and the ⋯ menu downloads them as subtitles (SRT or VTT). With the local AI on, each turn is labelled with who spoke, read from what was said (Name the speakers does it again). Kept as the browser recorded it (webm or ogg), or wav after a trim.

                                                                  Meetings, lectures and voice notes, kept as audio.

                                                                    Live captions

                                                                    Live captions write what the microphone hears as you go, on this computer: the audio goes to a small speech helper that runs here, never to the internet. The line at the bottom is still being written and settles after a pause; the three above it are done. Stop saves everything said as a note tagged captions, and Copy takes it without stopping. Translate, when the offline translator is installed (Settings, Packages), writes each finished line in Spanish under the captions; the note keeps what was said. With Keep the audio of live captions on (Settings, General, Microphone), Stop also keeps the audio in Library, Recordings, with these lines as its transcript. Start and stop them from the command palette, Live captions. They need a local speech helper; its row in Settings, Packages says what is missing.

                                                                      Dictionary

                                                                      Never flagged as typos, in any document.

                                                                      These words are stored with your notebook rather than in this browser, so they survive a cleared cache and they are the same in the desktop window and in a tab. Adding one here is the same as pressing "Add to dictionary" on a flagged word.

                                                                      The checks themselves are spelling, spacing, repeated words and sentence length, plus grammar (agreement, "a" or "an", its or it's and the like) from Harper, a grammar checker that runs on this computer, and an accessibility check (a skipped heading level, an image with no description, link text like "click here"). They skip code, addresses, file paths, email addresses, units after a number (10 min, 5 km) and the words of a link; "Check link text" below puts the link words back. They read the text, not its meaning. "Check with AI" in the suggestions panel is what reads for meaning.

                                                                      In a document, autocorrect and word suggestions are per document, in the editor's ⋯ menu; in notes, chat and titles autocorrect is one switch in Settings, General, Writing. Import takes a .txt file with one word per line and adds to the list; it never removes a word.

                                                                      Typing filters the list. Enter adds the word.

                                                                          Checking the models…

                                                                          Get it from ollama.com, then start it.

                                                                          Model backend

                                                                          Ollama powers the chat answers and auto-filing. Install it from ollama.com, start it, and this screen lights up. Capturing notes and keyword search work fine without it.

                                                                          The second option covers any server speaking the OpenAI API: LM Studio, llama.cpp's server, Jan and vLLM are all the same choice, differing only by address. Leave the address blank for the usual one (Ollama :11434, LM Studio :1234/v1); fill it in if you started the server on your own port.

                                                                          Leave the address blank for the server's usual port.

                                                                          Chat model

                                                                          Answers your questions, and switches instantly.

                                                                          The context window is how much of your conversation and notes the model can hold at once, counted in tokens. Empty means auto: the app uses what the model file or your server reports.

                                                                          Set a number when you know better than the file does, for example when you started llama.cpp with a larger window, or when you want to hold a big model to a smaller one so it loads faster and uses less memory. The setting is remembered per model, so a small model and a large one can differ.

                                                                          Utility model

                                                                          A small fast model does the filing, the digest and writing fixes, so the chat model stays free.

                                                                          Quick background jobs run on this model, so a big slow chat model isn't tied up categorising every note. Point it at a small fast model (e.g. llama3.2) and let a bigger one answer your questions. Leave as “Same as chat model” to keep it simple.

                                                                          Vision model

                                                                          Used for images in chat. Auto-detect picks one that can see.

                                                                          “Auto-detect” uses the first installed model that reports it can see images. Pick one by hand if you have several, or if auto-detect isn't finding the one you want.

                                                                          Reading text

                                                                          OCR for scanned PDFs and text in images. Automatic prefers a dedicated reader.

                                                                          Left on “Automatic”, this prefers a document reader (GLM-OCR, DeepSeek-OCR, PaddleOCR-VL) when you have one installed, then falls back to your vision model. Scanned PDFs also need the “Read scanned PDFs” extra, in Settings, Packages.

                                                                          Model per feature

                                                                          Each of these runs on the model it inherits until you give it one of its own.

                                                                          A feature left on “inherited” follows the chat model above, or the utility model where the feature is a background one, so changing your chat model changes it too. Give one a model of its own when the job is different: a bigger model for drafting, a small quick one for the Guide.

                                                                          The Chat tab, the Ask tab and the Writing room each have the same choice in a dropdown beside where you type. It is the same setting: change it in either place and the other follows.

                                                                          Reset on a row hands that feature back to what it inherits. The button below does the same for every feature at once and says how many it will clear.

                                                                          Advanced response settings

                                                                          Each row starts at what the model recommends for itself.

                                                                          How the model picks its words. Each row starts at what this model recommends for itself, change one only if you have a reason, and Reset puts it back.

                                                                          Installed models

                                                                          Each model's menu puts it to use or removes it to free up disk; one in use says for what.

                                                                          Test my models

                                                                          Runs your installed models on your own notes and recommends one.

                                                                          Each model files a sample of your notes, answers a question about each one from three notes shown to it, and calls a search tool five times. Filing is right when it picks the category you chose; an answer is right when it names the note the question came from.

                                                                          Everything runs on this computer, against the model server you set above. Forty notes over two models takes a few minutes to half an hour. Stop ends the run; a stopped run makes no recommendation.

                                                                            Suggested downloads

                                                                            Models Ollama can download for you.

                                                                            Each card says how much memory the model asks for and whether that fits this computer: Fits is under 60% of its memory, Tight is up to 85%, and Too big is more than that. A graphics card whose own memory holds the model counts instead of the system memory, and memory that is free only right now can take a Fits down to Tight. The line above the cards shows what was detected; Edit corrects it when it is wrong.

                                                                            Sizes with a ~ are the download size we shipped and have not checked; they turn exact once the model is installed. The starting pick in each group is ours, chosen for being small and dependable, not the result of a benchmark.

                                                                            Pick a dedicated embedding model (e.g. nomic-embed-text): chat models can't create embeddings. Changing this re-reads every note so search keeps making sense. It runs in the background (Settings, Background tasks shows it, with Stop) and search keeps using the current model until the new one has read every note.

                                                                            Embedding models lists the choices with their size, languages, how much text they read at once and their licence. Use switches in one press for an open licence; others link to their terms. Each row's menu installs, reinstalls or uninstalls it (never the one in use). A model with only some of its files says Files missing and offers Reinstall; the app also repairs the one search uses as a background task.

                                                                            Found on this computer lists embedding models already on disk (the Hugging Face cache, Ollama, LM Studio), read without going online. Pull a model by name checks a Hugging Face repo or an Ollama name online when you press Pull, then downloads it as a background task.

                                                                            The built-in engine runs inside Tessellate, so the app holds it in memory while it is open: about 300 MB with the default model. With Ollama the model lives in Ollama instead and Tessellate itself stays near 100 MB.

                                                                            Off, search uses keywords. About 130 MB, once, from huggingface.co and pypi.org.

                                                                            Search by meaning needs one Python package, fastembed, which brings ONNX Runtime with it (no PyTorch), and a small model from huggingface.co: about 130 MB in all, downloaded once, and it needs the internet. Tessellate asks before it downloads anything. Turn this on and it starts at once, in the background (Settings, Background tasks shows it, with Stop); search uses keywords until it finishes.

                                                                            After an upgrade from a version that ran on PyTorch, the old model files do not work with the new engine, so this is one download that replaces them. Your notes keep their search data (BGE Small, Multilingual E5 Small) or are read again in the background (any other model). Once the new model is ready, Embedding models, Old search files lists what the old engine left on this computer, with Remove.

                                                                            Off, nothing is downloaded and search by keywords keeps working. You can still install it yourself from Settings, Packages, or pick an Ollama embedding model below instead.

                                                                            Pick a dedicated embedding model, chat models can't create embeddings.

                                                                                  Search index

                                                                                  Rebuilds both halves of search: the word index that finds exact words, and what semantic search matches on. Worth doing after an update or a restore, or if searching stops finding notes you know are there. It re-reads every note with its category, tags and attached text included.

                                                                                  Rebuilds the word index and what semantic search matches on.

                                                                                  Search relevance

                                                                                  Minimum similarity: a semantic match below this score is dropped, however few results that leaves. Above-average margin: on top of that floor, a note also has to beat the rest of this search's own results by this many standard deviations: the app's own defence against a model that scores everything in a narrow band, so a flat floor alone lets unrelated notes through. Raise either number for fewer, more confident results; lower them if search feels too strict. Reset to default undoes both.

                                                                                  Personas

                                                                                  A persona is Atlas's voice; pick the active one in the Chat tab.

                                                                                  Each persona is a name and a set of instructions that shape how Atlas talks: its tone, what it leads with, what it avoids. New persona writes one; the Chat tab's persona menu picks which one answers. The answer style below applies whichever persona is active.

                                                                                    Answer style

                                                                                    How Atlas words its answers, whichever persona is active.

                                                                                    With no model, Atlas answers from your notes in this voice; the facts are the same in each.

                                                                                    With no model running, Atlas answers from your notes in its own words. Warm and concise talks to you plainly; Neutral reads like a record; Playful is lighter; Plain says only what it must. The facts, their order and the sources are the same in every voice, and the line above shows a sample.

                                                                                    A pattern, a plan gone quiet or a change of mind, measured in your notes.

                                                                                    After an answer about a topic, Atlas can add a line the notes on the right cannot show you: a subject that keeps coming up, a plan no later note picks up, a change of mind. Each is counted from your own notes and carries Confirm and Not right. Every Not right raises the bar, so the more you dismiss, the fewer and closer the lines it adds.

                                                                                    Dashboard greeting

                                                                                    Give the dashboard's welcome message its own persona, independent of whichever one is active in Chat and search.

                                                                                    Add your own

                                                                                    Write {ai_name} where the name should go and it is replaced with Atlas. Optional.

                                                                                    Share

                                                                                    Skills

                                                                                    A skill is a job you can run with one click from the Chat tab.

                                                                                    A skill is a job you can run with one click from the Chat tab: what to do, the steps to do it in, the tools it's allowed to use, and anything it should ask you for first. Naming its tools is what makes a small model actually reach for them, and only those tools are offered while it runs. Destructive steps still ask for your approval.

                                                                                    A skill can also be a Markdown file in the skills folder named under the list: the file's name is the skill's name, the text is what it should do, and a "## Steps" list gives its steps. Front matter can set the description, the tools and the inputs. A file saved there is listed without a restart; edit or delete it in the folder.

                                                                                    Your skills

                                                                                      Add your own
                                                                                      Tools this skill may use (optional)

                                                                                      Ticking a few leaves far more room in a small model's context.

                                                                                      Leave everything unticked to let it use whatever is switched on in Settings, Tools it can use. Ticking a few is both safer and more reliable: they're the only ones offered for the run, which leaves far more room in a small model's context.

                                                                                      Check it worked (optional)

                                                                                      When the run ends, the app reads one number back out of your notebook and checks it.

                                                                                      A model can report having done something it did not do. This is the app's own answer: after the last step it runs a counting tool itself and compares the number, so "I tagged them" becomes "no note is left untagged". Pick a tool the skill is allowed to use, then what the count should be. Unchanged compares against the reading taken before the run started, which is what a skill that only reads should promise. A run that stopped early is never reported as checked.

                                                                                      Templates

                                                                                      A template fills the Capture box with a starting shape you can pick from a dropdown.

                                                                                      A template fills the Capture box with a starting shape, a recipe's ingredient list, a meeting's agenda. A built-in one can be edited, and Reset brings the original back; your own can also be removed. Picking one from the Capture tab's dropdown never throws away text you've already typed there without asking first.

                                                                                      To put one into any editor where the cursor is, type insert template in the command palette (Ctrl+K) and pick it.

                                                                                        Add your own

                                                                                        {{date}} and {{time}} fill in now, {{clipboard}} what you copied, {{cursor}} where typing starts.

                                                                                        What it remembers

                                                                                        Standing instructions Atlas follows in every conversation, from either side.

                                                                                        Atlas can keep standing instructions, say "always answer in British English" and it will keep doing that in every conversation from then on. This is the whole list, and you can switch any of them off or delete them.

                                                                                        When Atlas spots one of these in conversation it suggests it rather than saving it: the suggestion appears in the chat with a yes/no, and again at the top of this list until you answer. Nothing reaches Atlas's instructions until you say yes.

                                                                                        Nothing saved yet. Tell Atlas a preference in chat and ask it to remember, and it will appear here.

                                                                                        What it learned

                                                                                        Everything Atlas worked out on its own, yours to correct, delete or switch off.

                                                                                        "What it remembers" is what you told it. This is what it worked out by itself while reading your notes: a claim it thinks a note makes, a question it thinks a note leaves open. Every row says which note it came from, which model decided it and how sure it was.

                                                                                        A model that is wrong quietly is worse than no model, so all of it is yours: edit a row and no later run overwrites it, delete one and the same thing is never worked out again, or switch the whole thing off and keep your notes exactly as they are.

                                                                                        "Learned from you" counts your corrections (a note moved to another category, a suggestion dismissed) and how many of the notes it filed itself you left where it put them: the older half of the last 200 against the newer half, so you can see whether your moves taught it anything.

                                                                                        What may run

                                                                                        Each of these reads your notes in the background. Off means it computes nothing and shows nothing.

                                                                                        What it worked out

                                                                                        One row per thing derived, newest first.

                                                                                        0 selected

                                                                                          Nothing worked out yet. This fills in as Atlas reads your notes in the background.

                                                                                          All of it at once

                                                                                          Read it outside the app, or throw it away. Your notes are never touched by either.

                                                                                          What Atlas may do in Agent mode; risky changes ask you first.

                                                                                          How many are offered at once

                                                                                          Sending only the tools a message needs leaves more room for your notes.

                                                                                          Every tool Atlas is offered is described to it again on every round of every message, all of them together are about three quarters of what a small model reads before it even sees your question. Sending only the ones a message plausibly needs leaves far more room for your notes.

                                                                                          Small model mode

                                                                                          Offers a small model one tool at a time instead of the whole set.

                                                                                          A model under about 8 billion parameters does far better with one tool in front of it than with twenty. In this mode each step of a skill is offered only the tool that step needs, with a worked example of the call.

                                                                                          When to use it Auto reads the size out of the chat model's own name (qwen3:4b is small, llama3.3:70b is not). A name with no size in it means "no idea", and no idea means off.

                                                                                          Run budget

                                                                                          What one skill run may spend before it stops and reports.

                                                                                          A run is one turn per step, plus a retry for a step that did not do what it said and up to two rewrites. Each of those starts with a fresh allowance of tool-calling rounds, so a run that goes wrong does not loop, it grinds. The budget is what ends that. A run that reaches it stops between rounds, says so, and shows what it changed with a way to put it back. Set either to 0 for no limit.

                                                                                          The token figure is per step, so a nine step skill gets nine times it. There is no time limit out of the box: a local model is slow, and slow is not the same as wrong. A nine step skill measured on a 4B model took twenty three minutes to reach step three, and a ninety second run budget had already ended it.

                                                                                          Tokens per step Multiplied by the number of steps in the run.
                                                                                          Seconds Wall time for the whole run. 0, and off, unless you set one.

                                                                                          Which ones it may use

                                                                                          Turn one off and Atlas is never offered it.

                                                                                            No tool matches that.

                                                                                            Use these tools from another app

                                                                                            Paste this into an MCP client's settings to let it read and write this notebook.

                                                                                            MCP is a standard way for an app such as Claude Desktop to use another program's tools. This snippet starts Tessellate's tool server on this computer, using the same notebook and the same Tools it can use switches as Atlas.

                                                                                            It also offers your notes to read and your skills as ready prompts. Risky changes such as deleting are never offered to another app, and private notes are never shown. The packaged app starts the same server with its --mcp option.

                                                                                            Effects & accessibility
                                                                                            
                
              
                                                                                            
              
                                                                                            
                
                                                                                            
                  Two switches, two kinds of motion. Reduce motion stills the
                  large movement: Atlas, the background art, the graph's
                  layout and the whiteboard, and so does your system's
                  reduced-motion setting.
                
                                                                                            
                
                                                                                            
                  Interface animations are the short ones that say what
                  happened: a button pressing in, a menu or dialog opening from
                  where you clicked, a tab's marker sliding to the new tab, a
                  list settling, a toast arriving. They are on by default and
                  play even with Reduce motion on; turn them off and every one
                  of them is instant.
                
                                                                                            
                
                                                                                            
                  The app's logo answers both: its top cell settles into place
                  once, then breathes slowly, and its cells lift in turn while
                  Atlas works. Either switch off holds it still.
                
                                                                                            
                
                                                                                            
                  Reveal replies is one of them: a reply written with no model
                  (from your notes, or the Guide's own help) rises into place a
                  block at a time in Chat, Ask, the popup agent and the Guide.
                  Reduce motion makes it a quick fade; off, it simply appears.
                
                                                                                            
              
                                                                                            

              
                                                                                            
                
                                                                                            
                  Performance mode
                  Flat panels, still background, slower graph physics. Auto: on for a machine with 2 cores or 4 GB or fewer.

                                                                                            Packages
                                                                                            
                
              
                                                                                            
              
                                                                                            Things Tessellate can do with one more package installed.
                                                                                            
              
                                                                                            
                
                                                                                            
                  Things Tessellate can do with one more package installed.
                  Nothing here is needed to write, search, tag or organise
                  your notes, each one turns on a feature that is otherwise
                  switched off, and everything is downloaded from PyPI to
                  this machine.
                
                                                                                            
                
                                                                                            
                  A bundle is the packages one kind of work needs together:
                  its Install fetches the ones still missing, and its ...
                  menu reinstalls or removes them all. Tick packages to act on
                  several at once from the bar above the list. They run one
                  after another, each says how it went, and one that fails
                  does not stop the rest. An installed package's ... menu has
                  Reinstall, for a feature that is switched on but not
                  working, and Remove. A notice that says a feature needs a
                  package has an Open Packages button that brings you to
                  that package's row.

                                                                                                  Give this command a key in your system's keyboard settings to capture a note over any app.
                                                                                                  
              
                                                                                                  
                
                                                                                                  
                  Windows: a desktop shortcut with this command as its target,
                  then its Properties, Shortcut key.
                  macOS: Shortcuts, a Run Shell Script action, then a keyboard
                  shortcut. Linux: your desktop's Keyboard settings, a custom

                  Every search box offers what you searched for before, then
                  the titles, tags and categories of your own notes that start
                  with your words. Tab, or Right at the end of the words, takes
                  the grey text; Down and Up walk the list, Enter takes the lit
                  one, Escape closes it. Shift+Delete removes a lit recent
                  search. Nothing is sent anywhere: it is built from this
                  notebook, and remembered on this device. Settings, Import
                  & export, Clear and forget clears the recent searches in
                  every box at once.
